# @aszura/saltline-browser

> The browser half of Saltline's connect and sign-in flows. It makes a PKCE pair on click, keeps
> the verifier (with the provider and your state) in that tab's `sessionStorage`, navigates to the
> provider, and on return hands the provider and verifier to your backend. It never talks to
> Saltline and never sees the API key. Includes optional React bindings at
> `@aszura/saltline-browser/react`. No dependencies.

This file is for AI coding assistants. Follow the rules first; the reference follows.

## Rules

1. **This package only calls two endpoints you mount on your own backend**: a start endpoint and
   a finish endpoint. `@aszura/saltline-node` (`connectFlow` / `signInFlow`) and `saltline/php`
   (`ConnectFlow` / `SignInFlow`) ship both, ready to mount; prefer them over hand-written
   endpoints. Never put a Saltline API key in browser code and never call `api.saltline.dev` from
   the browser.
2. **`start` needs `provider`** (e.g. `'google'`). The package sends it to start, keeps it with the
   verifier, and sends it to finish. Do not store the provider in your own session or a pending
   table: the finish payload carries it.
3. **Start endpoint contract:** receives JSON
   `{ provider, codeChallenge, codeChallengeMethod: 'S256', ...body }`, checks `provider` against
   an allowlist, calls `connections.init` (or `sessions.init`) with its own `auth` and
   `redirectUrl`, and answers `{ authorizationUrl, connectionKey }` (or
   `{ authorizationUrl, sessionKey }`).
4. **Finish endpoint contract:** receives JSON `{ provider, connectionKey, codeVerifier, ...body }`
   (or `sessionKey`), calls `claim(provider, key, codeVerifier)`, stores the result against the
   logged-in user, and answers any JSON. That answer becomes `result.data`.
5. **Carry app context with `state`, not the URL or your session.** `start({ state })` is kept in
   the tab and comes back as `result.state` from `finish`. JSON only; it is never sent anywhere.
6. **Same tab start to finish.** `sessionStorage` is per tab. The provider must redirect back to
   the tab that started the flow (normal redirects do). Don't open the authorization URL in a new
   tab or popup.
7. **`finish` is one-shot.** It deletes the pending flow before POSTing, so a reload can't replay
   it. It's safe to call on every load of the redirect page; it returns `null` on an ordinary visit.
8. **With a client-side router, pass `cleanUrl`.** The default `history.replaceState` is invisible
   to React Router and Next.js. `cleanUrl: (path) => navigate(path, { replace: true })` (React
   Router) or `cleanUrl: (path) => router.replace(path)` (Next.js) keeps the router in sync.
9. **Next.js App Router: client components only.** `useSaltlineFinish`, `useSaltlineStart` and
   `SaltlineButton` need `'use client'` at the top of the file that uses them.
10. Both endpoints should sit behind your normal login/CSRF protection. Requests use
    `credentials: 'same-origin'` by default; pass CSRF tokens through `headers`.
11. **If the app already has an HTTP client** (axios instance, bearer tokens, refresh, `{ data }`
    envelopes), pass `send` instead of `url`. Do not write a fake-`Response` `fetch` adapter.
    `send(payload)` delivers the payload however the backend wants it and resolves the endpoint's
    JSON. For `start` that must be `{ authorizationUrl, connectionKey | sessionKey }` at the top
    level, so unwrap envelopes and rename fields inside `send`. `send` excludes `url`, `headers`,
    `credentials` and `fetch`. `bind()`, `data-saltline-start` and the script tag's `data-finish`
    only support `url`.

## Install

```sh
npm install @aszura/saltline-browser
```

No-build alternative: `<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@aszura/saltline-browser/dist/saltline.min.js"></script>`
sets `window.Saltline`, auto-binds `[data-saltline-start]` buttons, and runs `finish` if the tag has
`data-finish="/your/finish/endpoint"`.

## Vanilla usage

```ts
import { start, finish, SaltlineError } from '@aszura/saltline-browser';

// Connect button:
button.addEventListener('click', () => {
  start({ url: '/saltline/start', provider: 'google', state: { returnTo: '/settings?tab=mail' } })
    .catch((error) => showError(error));
});

// Page at your redirectUrl:
try {
  const result = await finish<{ connected: boolean }, { returnTo: string }>({ url: '/saltline/finish' });
  if (result === null) {
    // not a Saltline redirect
  } else if (result.ok) {
    // result.kind: 'connection' | 'session', result.provider, result.key,
    // result.data (your endpoint's JSON), result.state (what start was given)
    location.replace(result.state.returnTo);
  } else {
    // user declined / provider error: result.error, result.errorMessage,
    // result.state (from the flow this tab started last, or undefined)
  }
} catch (error) {
  if (error instanceof SaltlineError && error.code === 'VERIFIER_NOT_FOUND') {
    // started in another tab/browser, or already used. Start again.
  }
}
```

Through an existing HTTP client (`send` instead of `url`; one line each):

```ts
// GET with query params; backend answers { data: { authUrl, sessionKey } }
start({
  provider,
  send: (p) =>
    api.get(`auth/${p.provider}`, { params: { redirect: p.redirect, codeChallenge: p.codeChallenge } })
      .then((r) => ({ authorizationUrl: r.data.data.authUrl, sessionKey: r.data.data.sessionKey })),
  body: { redirect: '/signed-in' },
});

// POST through an authed client; backend answers { data: { authorizationUrl, connectionKey } }
start({ provider, send: (p) => api.post(`/integrations/init/${id}`, p).then((r) => r.data.data) });

// Claim through the same client; p already has provider, key and codeVerifier
finish({ send: (p) => api.post('auth', p).then((r) => r.data) });
```

Declarative buttons (with `bind()` from a bundle, or automatic with the script build):

```html
<button data-saltline-start="/saltline/start" data-saltline-provider="google"
        data-saltline-state="settings" data-saltline-integration-key="abc">Connect Google</button>
```

`data-saltline-provider` is the provider, `data-saltline-state` the state (a string), and every
other `data-saltline-*` attribute becomes a camelCase body field (`integrationKey`). While running,
the button has `aria-busy="true"`. It dispatches bubbling `saltline:started` (detail:
`StartResult`) or `saltline:error` (detail: the error). The script build's `data-finish` fires
`saltline:finished` (detail: `FinishResult`) or `saltline:error` on `document`.

## React

```tsx
'use client'; // Next.js App Router
import { SaltlineButton, useSaltlineStart, useSaltlineFinish } from '@aszura/saltline-browser/react';

<SaltlineButton url="/saltline/start" provider="google" state={{ returnTo: '/settings' }} onError={(e) => toast(String(e))}>
  Connect Google
</SaltlineButton>;

function Connected() {
  const navigate = useNavigate(); // React Router; Next.js: const router = useRouter() from 'next/navigation'
  const { loading, result, error } = useSaltlineFinish<{ connected: boolean }, { returnTo: string }>({
    url: '/saltline/finish',
    cleanUrl: (path) => navigate(path, { replace: true }), // Next.js: router.replace(path)
  });
  if (loading) return <p>Finishing…</p>;
  if (error) return <p>Something went wrong. Try connecting again.</p>;
  if (result?.ok === false) return <p>{result.errorMessage ?? 'Cancelled.'}</p>;
  if (result?.ok) return <Navigate to={result.state.returnTo} />;
  return null;
}
```

- `SaltlineButton`: `<button>` that runs `start` on click with its `provider`, `state` and `body`
  props. It is disabled and `aria-busy` while pending. Other props pass through to the button, and
  `type` defaults to `button`. An `onClick` that calls `preventDefault()` cancels the start. Takes
  `url` or `send` (never forwarded to the DOM).
- `useSaltlineStart(options)` returns `{ start(provider, { state?, body? }), pending, error }`.
  One hook serves a whole menu of providers. `start` never throws: failures go to `error` and
  `onError`, and it resolves `undefined`. Takes `url` or `send`.
- `useSaltlineFinish(options)` runs `finish` once on mount (StrictMode-safe) and returns
  `{ loading, result, error }`. Pass `enabled: false` to defer, e.g. until your auth has loaded.
  Takes `url` or `send`, plus `body` and `cleanUrl`. An inline `send` that changes every render is
  fine.
- React ≥ 16.8 is an optional peer dependency. Only the `/react` entry point imports it.

## API reference

```ts
// Endpoint options: exactly one of these two shapes (TypeScript enforces it; neither or both
// rejects with a TypeError).
type FetchEndpointOptions = {
  url: string;                          // your endpoint, POSTed as JSON
  headers?: HeadersInit;                // e.g. CSRF token
  credentials?: RequestCredentials;     // default 'same-origin'
  fetch?: typeof fetch;
};
type SendEndpointOptions = {
  send: (payload: Record<string, unknown>) => Promise<unknown>; // resolve the endpoint's JSON
};

start(options: (FetchEndpointOptions | SendEndpointOptions) & {
  provider: string;                     // required; sent to start and finish
  state?: unknown;                      // JSON; comes back as finish's result.state
  body?: Record<string, unknown>;       // extra payload fields; provider wins on conflict
  navigate?: ((url: string) => void) | false; // default location.assign; false = don't navigate
}): Promise<{ kind: 'connection' | 'session'; provider: string; key: string; authorizationUrl: string }>

finish<T, S>(options: (FetchEndpointOptions | SendEndpointOptions) & {
  body?: Record<string, unknown>;       // extra payload fields; provider, key and codeVerifier win on conflict
  location?: string | URL;              // default location.href
  cleanUrl?: boolean | ((path: string) => void); // default true unless `location` given; a function gets
                                        // the clean path+search+hash to replace through your router
}): Promise<
  | { ok: true; kind: 'connection' | 'session'; provider: string; key: string; data: T; state: S }
  | { ok: false; error: string; errorMessage: string | null; state: S | undefined }
  | null                                // not a Saltline redirect
>

bind(root?: ParentNode = document, defaults?: { headers?; credentials?; fetch?; navigate? }): () => void  // returns unbind; url only
createPkce(): Promise<{ codeVerifier; codeChallenge; codeChallengeMethod: 'S256' }>
parseRedirect(url): { ok: true; kind; key } | { ok: false; error; errorMessage } | null
redirectPath(url): string               // path + search + hash without Saltline's params
```

`start` only navigates to `http(s)` URLs. It rejects anything else with `INVALID_START_RESPONSE`.
Pending flows older than one hour are cleaned up the next time `start` runs; a declined redirect
drops the flow this tab started last.

## Errors

`start` and `finish` throw `SaltlineError` with `code`, `status` (endpoint HTTP status or null) and
`body` (endpoint response, parsed if JSON). Branch on `code`:

| code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `START_FAILED` | Start endpoint answered non-2xx or was unreachable, or `send` rejected. |
| `INVALID_START_RESPONSE` | Start endpoint's answer lacked an http(s) `authorizationUrl` or a `connectionKey`/`sessionKey`. |
| `FINISH_FAILED` | Finish endpoint answered non-2xx or was unreachable, or `send` rejected. Start the flow again. |
| `STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE` | `sessionStorage` blocked (some private modes, sandboxed iframes). |
| `VERIFIER_NOT_FOUND` | This tab didn't start a flow for the key in the URL, or it was already used. |

When `send` rejects, the original error is `cause`. `status`/`body` are taken from `err.status`/`err.body`,
else axios-style `err.response.status`/`err.response.data`, else `null`. A `SaltlineError` thrown by
`send` is rethrown unchanged.

With the SDK-provided endpoints, `body` of a `FINISH_FAILED` / `START_FAILED` is
`{ code, error, requestId? }`: `UNKNOWN_PROVIDER` or `INVALID_INPUT` (400), a claim Saltline
refused such as `CODE_VERIFIER_MISMATCH` or `CONNECTION_NOT_FOUND` (400: start again), or any other
Saltline code (502).

A provider-side failure or a user who declined is not thrown: `finish` returns
`{ ok: false, error, errorMessage, state }`.

## Server side

Node (Express), with `@aszura/saltline-node`:

```ts
import { Saltline, connectFlow } from '@aszura/saltline-node';
const saltline = new Saltline({ apiKey: process.env.SALTLINE_API_KEY! });
const connect = connectFlow(saltline, { providers: ['google', 'trello'], redirectUrl: 'https://yourapp.com/connected' });

app.post('/saltline/start', requireLogin, connect.express.start((req) => ({ externalUserId: req.user.id })));
app.post('/saltline/finish', requireLogin, connect.express.finish(async ({ connection }, req) => {
  await db.saveConnection(req.user.id, connection.connectionKey);
  return { connected: true };
}));
```

Next.js App Router / Remix / Hono / SvelteKit / Workers: `export const POST = connect.web.start(...)`
and `connect.web.finish(...)`, `Request` in and `Response` out. Sign-in: `signInFlow` with the same
shape; the claim result has `user` and `raw`.

PHP, with `saltline/php`:

```php
$connect = new Saltline\ConnectFlow($saltline, ['google', 'trello'], 'https://yourapp.com/connected');
$connect->serveStart(externalUserId: (string) $user->id);                  // POST /saltline/start
$connect->serveFinish(fn (array $claimed) => saveAndAnswer($claimed));     // POST /saltline/finish
// Frameworks: $connect->replyStart($input, $externalUserId) / replyFinish($input, $onClaimed)
// return ['status' => int, 'body' => array]. Sign-in: Saltline\SignInFlow.
```
